mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous year's average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods meeting both GDPC1 and HOUST trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% for three consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and corporate earnings momentum, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA by >1.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows at a pace above its 12-month average signals a tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS > 12-month average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE < 4% and above-average PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% combined with a concurrent decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% for two months signals a risk of deflationary monetary policy, which can depress growth expectations and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both CPIAUCSL < 2% and FEDFUNDS < 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% signals a rebound in consumer spending, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA by >3% for one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when RSAFS surges above its 12-month MA by >3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month and a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below its 12-month average signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp AND PAYEMS < 12-month average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both UNRATE rises > 0.5pp and PAYEMS falls below its 12-month average in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its previous month's value for six consecutive months signals persistent manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods where INDPRO rises for six consecutive months.
